samples.title: Type 2 diabetes follow-up with kidney disease
samples.transcript:
[doctor] Good morning. How have you been since your last visit?

[patient] Pretty tired, honestly. And I've been getting up at night to pee two or three times.

[doctor] Okay. Let's go through your diabetes first. Have you been taking the metformin, 1000 milligrams twice a day?

[patient] Most days. I miss the evening one sometimes.

[doctor] Any low blood sugars, shakiness, or sweating?

[patient] No, nothing like that. My morning readings are usually around 160 to 180.

[doctor] That's higher than we want. Any numbness or tingling in your feet?

[patient] A little tingling in my toes, mostly at night.

[doctor] Any swelling in your legs or foamy urine?

[patient] My ankles swell by the end of the day. And yes, the urine has looked foamy lately.

[doctor] Your blood pressure today is 148 over 90 and your weight is up two kilograms. Your last lab showed your kidney function has dropped, with an eGFR of 52, so this is stage 3 chronic kidney disease from the diabetes.

[patient] Is that serious?

[doctor] It's manageable if we act now. I want to add lisinopril 10 milligrams once a day to protect your kidneys and lower your pressure, and I'm ordering a urine albumin test and repeat blood work in four weeks.

[patient] Should I change my diet?

[doctor] Yes, less salt and fewer refined carbohydrates. I'll refer you to the dietitian. Come back in one month.

samples.title: Low back pain after lifting
samples.transcript:
[doctor] What brings you in today?

[patient] My lower back has been killing me since Saturday. I was moving a couch.

[doctor] Where exactly is the pain, and does it go down your legs?

[patient] Right across the lower back, mostly on the left. It doesn't go down my leg, but it's worse when I bend forward.

[doctor] Any numbness, weakness in your legs, or trouble controlling your bladder or bowels?

[patient] No, none of that.

[doctor] Any fever, weight loss, or history of back problems?

[patient] No fever. I had a similar episode about two years ago that went away on its own.

[doctor] On a scale of one to ten, how bad is it?

[patient] About a six when I move, a three when I rest.

[doctor] On exam you have tenderness over the left lower back muscles, full strength in both legs, normal reflexes, and a negative straight leg raise test. This looks like a muscle strain, not a nerve problem.

[patient] Do I need an X-ray?

[doctor] Not right now, since there are no warning signs. I recommend ibuprofen 400 milligrams three times a day with food for one week, heat packs, and gentle walking. Avoid heavy lifting for two weeks.

[patient] And if it doesn't improve?

[doctor] Come back in two weeks, and we'll consider physical therapy and imaging.

samples.title: Child with an asthma flare-up
samples.transcript:
[doctor] Hello. Tell me what's been going on with your son.

[patient] He's been coughing and wheezing since yesterday, especially at night, and he's using his inhaler a lot.

[doctor] How old is he, and how often has he needed the inhaler?

[patient] He's seven. Every four hours or so since last night.

[doctor] Any fever or runny nose?

[patient] A runny nose for two days, no fever.

[doctor] Has he been short of breath playing, or is he able to talk in full sentences?

[patient] He gets winded walking up the stairs, but he can talk fine.

[doctor] Any triggers, like pets, smoke, or exercise?

[patient] His cousin visited with a cat last weekend.

[doctor] His oxygen saturation is 96 percent, his respiratory rate is 24, and I hear wheezing on both sides but good air movement. This is a mild asthma flare-up.

[patient] Does he need the hospital?

[doctor] No. We'll give an albuterol treatment here, then continue albuterol two puffs every four to six hours for the next few days, and start a short course of prednisolone, 20 milligrams once a day for three days.

[patient] Anything else?

[doctor] Keep him away from the cat, and see me in a week. Go to the emergency room if he can't speak in full sentences or his lips turn blue.

samples.title: Bladder infection
samples.transcript:
[doctor] What can I help you with today?

[patient] It burns when I pee and I feel like I have to go every few minutes. It started two days ago.

[doctor] Any blood in the urine, fever, chills, or pain in your sides?

[patient] No blood and no fever. Just some pressure low in my belly.

[doctor] Any nausea or vomiting, or vaginal discharge?

[patient] No to all of that.

[doctor] Have you had urinary infections before?

[patient] Once, about a year ago.

[doctor] Are you pregnant or could you be, and do you have any drug allergies?

[patient] No chance of being pregnant. I'm allergic to sulfa drugs.

[doctor] Your temperature is 98.4 and there's mild tenderness above the pubic bone, but no tenderness in your back. Your urine dipstick shows leukocytes and nitrites, so this is an uncomplicated bladder infection.

[patient] What do I take?

[doctor] Since you're allergic to sulfa, I'll prescribe nitrofurantoin 100 milligrams twice a day for five days. Drink plenty of water and avoid caffeine.

[patient] When should I worry?

[doctor] If you get fever, back pain, or vomiting, or if it isn't better in three days, call us right away.

samples.title: Sore throat (scripted retry demonstration)
samples.transcript:
[doctor] Hi there. What's going on?

[patient] I've had a really sore throat for three days, and it hurts to swallow.

[doctor] Any fever, cough, or runny nose?

[patient] I felt feverish last night, but no cough and no runny nose.

[doctor] Any swollen glands, rash, or trouble breathing?

[patient] My neck feels tender on both sides. No rash, and I can breathe fine.

[doctor] Has anyone at home been sick?

[patient] My daughter had strep throat last week.

[doctor] Your temperature is 100.9, your throat is red with white patches on both tonsils, and the glands in your neck are tender. The rapid strep test in the office is positive.

[patient] So it is strep?

[doctor] Yes. I'll start you on amoxicillin 500 milligrams twice a day for ten days. Take acetaminophen for the pain and fever, and drink plenty of fluids.

[patient] When can I go back to work?

[doctor] After you've been on the antibiotic for 24 hours and you have no fever. Call me if you aren't better in two days.

samples.title: Pelvic pain, suspected endometriosis
samples.transcript:
[doctor] Thanks for coming in. What's been troubling you?

[patient] I've had pain low in my belly for about eight months, and it gets much worse during my period.

[doctor] How would you describe the pain, and how bad does it get?

[patient] It's a deep cramping ache. On the worst days of my period it's an eight out of ten and I can't go to work.

[doctor] Is the pain only around your period, or is it there at other times too?

[patient] It's mostly during my period, but I get a duller ache in between, and sex has become painful.

[doctor] Are your periods heavy or irregular?

[patient] They're heavy, about seven days, and I pass clots on the second and third day.

[doctor] Any problems with your bowels or bladder, like pain when you go?

[patient] Sometimes it hurts to have a bowel movement during my period. Urinating is fine.

[doctor] Have you tried anything for the pain, and are you hoping to get pregnant?

[patient] Ibuprofen helps a little. We aren't trying for a baby right now, but we might want one in a couple of years.

[doctor] On exam your abdomen is soft with mild tenderness low on both sides. On the pelvic exam there is tenderness behind the uterus and the uterus doesn't move as freely as it should. This pattern of symptoms and findings is typical of endometriosis, and that is the diagnosis I'm giving you.

[patient] What happens next?

[doctor] I'm ordering a pelvic ultrasound to look for cysts. For now, take ibuprofen 600 milligrams with food three times a day during your period, and we'll start a hormonal treatment to reduce the bleeding and pain. I'll also refer you to a gynecologist to talk about a laparoscopy to confirm it. Come back in six weeks.
